svg.title: Launch Attention and Tenant Isolation Are Separate Tests
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-launch-and-isolation-observations; chapter number: 4; title: Launch Attention and Tenant Isolation Are Separate Tests; subtitle: Audience response does not establish authorization safety, and a concurrency exercise does not establish market demand.; caption: Jack Smith reports Product Hunt launch observations; Alex Rusin reports a configuration-specific Prisma concurrency test.; assumptions note: Each low and high repeats the same reported observation, not an estimated range. Jack Smith's upvotes, video audience, and hours cannot be added to Alex Rusin's request count or interpreted as shares of a common total.; note: Alex Rusin limits the no-contamination result to the tested configuration and failure mode. Past The Diagram recommends testing isolation through the actual application role rather than relying on a privileged owner's apparent success.; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: No additive total; separate observations in upvotes, video views, hours, and concurrent requests; buckets: label: Product Hunt launch result; low: 17; high: 17; notes: 17 upvotes reported by Jack Smith, used as the benchmark to beat on the next attempt.; label: Bespoke launch video audience; low: 2; high: 2; notes: Two views reported by Jack Smith after hours of production; they preferred reallocating effort toward more engaging outbound content.; label: Hidden-vote opening period; low: 4; high: 4; notes: Jack Smith describes the first four hours with hidden vote totals and randomized product ordering.; label: Prisma concurrency exercise; low: 800; high: 800; notes: Alex Rusin reports 800 concurrent requests with no contamination in the tested configuration.
